content.content:
Haj-Wan: "I wait for Sei-Wan, my kin. He walked out into the basin alone, to prove himself to the Agaceph, and he has not come back. I am Agaceph too. By our custom none of us may follow a walk-out, so I stay at this gate. An outsider may follow him. He went east from the gate through the shallows, and he is up among the roots there. Vipers lie in the roots, and the mud holds anyone who stands still. Nothing that walks in the basin lives long. Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden beside me, will say the same. I want him alive. He wants the walk-out to count, and it counts only if he comes home on his own feet. If another brings him in, the Agaceph will say he did not finish. I would have him alive and shamed sooner than proud and dead. Bring him home if you must. But if he can walk, let the walk-out be his own."

content.text:
I finished the one quest in this game, The Gates of Helstrom, and the journal now shows nothing active.

- **The hook:** Haj-Wan, a guard at the gate, said her kin Sei-Wan had walked out into the basin to prove himself to the Agaceph tribe and hadn't come back.
- **The search:** I found Sei-Wan up in the roots in the shallows east of the gate. He wouldn't come down while a viper lay between him and home.
- **The fight:** I killed the viper.
- **The choice:** I could talk him home, which would cost him the walk-out. Instead I told him to walk home on his own feet and said nothing at the gate. He keeps his honor and is alive, but Haj-Wan is still waiting and doesn't know.

I submitted my closing take. It said the quest was clear and the choice was the best part, but the ending felt abrupt. I also noted that two of the persuade options looked like duplicates.
